suspects.name: Cook
suspects.statement: "I just used ls and cd to grab supplies from the back room -- didn't even know there were hidden files on that terminal until someone from IT mentioned it."
suspects.clue: A shift log left open on the terminal shows the same crew member badged into the Cafeteria twice within one hour -- once more than their schedule allows.

suspects.name: Clerk
suspects.statement: "I only ever edit the crew directory through the front-end form -- I wouldn't know a robots.txt file from a grocery list."
suspects.clue: The hidden staging page still lists the Admin Assistant as the last person to edit the crew directory, timestamped the night of the incident.

suspects.name: Guard
suspects.statement: "My panel's login has never used a default password. I changed it myself the day it was installed -- I'd bet my badge on it."
suspects.clue: The dumped session log shows the Security Officer disabled the corridor camera outside the Lab twelve minutes before the incident was reported.

suspects.name: Hauler
suspects.statement: "That crate label was just routine stock code, scrambled text or not -- I sign out whatever's on the manifest, no questions asked."
suspects.clue: The decoded manifest shows the crate was signed out by the Storage Technician, who had no clearance for lab equipment that day.

suspects.name: Researcher
suspects.statement: "I don't go digging up birthdays or backgrounds on people online -- that's not something I'd waste my shift doing."
suspects.clue: The unlocked record shows the Lab Scientist ran an off-the-books background check on a crewmate the same night, then filed the results under a fake name.
